exercises.title: Remove duplicates in place
exercises.task: Same direction this time: a slow pointer marks where the next kept value goes, a fast one reads ahead. Fill the loop of Dedup: it compacts a sorted slice in place and returns how many values it kept.
hints: The first value is always kept: start with k := 1 (when the slice is not empty).
For each i from 1: if a[i] differs from the last kept value a[k-1], copy it to a[k] and move k.
No new slice: the point is O(1) extra memory. The caller uses a[:k].

exercises.title: Merge two processor traces
exercises.task: A tracer records what each processor does in its own buffer, sorted by time: one shared buffer would make the processors wait for each other at every event. To read the program's story you need one timeline. Merge returns all the events in time order, in O(n + m), without sorting. On equal times, the event from a comes first.
hints: One index into each slice. Take the smaller of a[i] and b[j], append it, move that index.
When one list is used up, append the rest of the other one.
"On equal times A first": take from a when a[i].T <= b[j].T. That makes the merge stable, which matters for merge sort (A6).
